newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SAMPRAS REJECTS PLAYING IN DAVIS CUP TIE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS REJECTS PLAYING IN DAVIS CUP TIE.

text.p: World number-one Pete Sampras will not play in the Davis Cup when the United States meets The Netherlands in a second round tie in California in April, Sampras said on Friday.
Sampras said playing the tie would mean seven straight weeks of tennis for him and could hamper his preparation for the French Open.

Sampras told U.S. captain Tom Gullikson he would make himself available for the third-round tie should the U.S. win, but he doesn't want to endanger his chances of maintaining the number one ranking and winning Grand Slam titles this year.
"After playing Palermo (a second round tie against Italy in 1995), I was burnt out and I promised myself I wouldn't do it again," Sampras said.
Sampras, who led the United States to the Davis Cup title in 1995, said he is confident the team can overcome the Netherlands without him.
"Absolutely," he said. "American tennis is the strongest in the world."
Andre Agassi said on Friday he won't make a decision on playing the tie until he speaks to Gullikson.
Number 4 ranked Michael Chang has told Gullikson he would like to play. Jim Courier and Todd Martin are also possibilities.
Alex O'Brien, who with Richey Reneberg lost their doubles match in the U.S.'s victory over Brazil, also may be named.
